name: LIFT OFF
summary: Level 1, dl 0-90: the two verbs and the shard, unlocking SECOND RING (dl 12), TWIN SHARDS (18) and THIRD RING (40); opens on world DRIFT.
detail: LV row 1. key:1 is the reference key every other level's ratio is measured against. Guarantees here are the POW_INTRO trio shield->slow-mo->nova, ordered and once per run (G.introN). Its finish line at dl 90 runs the star dive; a first-ever run passes through its card, a returning player's level-1 start and retry are instant.

name: INTO THE RINGS
summary: Level 2, dl 90-215: the ring threats, unlocking GATES (100), DRIFTERS (128) and SHUTTERS (165); guarantees hypernova and slipstream; opens on world TIDE.
detail: LV row 2. Its card is two lines that say what the level IS - the earlier card previewed gates, drifters and shutters at dl 90, up to 75 seconds before the first one existed. The hypernova is the first post-curriculum placement (G.hyperPlaced) and slipstream follows it; both are once per RUN and pre-spent for a run that opens past level 2.

name: THE STORM
summary: Level 3, dl 215-340: the two compounds and the saucer, unlocking SLIDING GATES (240), THE SAUCER (275) and SHUTTER PAIRS (310); guarantees magnet and star trail.
detail: LV row 3. Three shapes ~35 dl apart, the spacing level 2 already used; the shutter pair moved 295->310 to keep it. The saucer's slot is the last one with room for its lesson, because a tier banner may not fire inside a level's endgame window. Level 3 is also the floor for the black hole's ordinary 5% roll.

name: EVENT HORIZON
summary: Level 4, dl 340-470: DIVERS at dl 395 - the first formation taught above dl 340 - plus the black hole's one guaranteed offer and THE MIRROR; opens on world GLASS.
detail: LV row 4. It was the endless level and now has a finish line; it keeps its identity as the black hole's level. dl 340 is also the floor every late-board rule is gated at: the SHAPE_RANK weighting ramp, the two-pair twin ceiling and the gap-floor decay all start here, so levels 1-3 are untouched by construction rather than by inspection.

name: REDSHIFT
summary: Level 5, dl 470-610: THE NARROWS at dl 520 and scorch; its own end (610) is what warnTime() reads as the endless level's floor.
detail: LV row 5. THE NARROWS is the last thing the game teaches and the mirror of GATES - one wall each for the two verbs, 420 difficulty-seconds apart. warnTime() derives examDl as LV[LEVEL_MAX-2].end rather than a literal, which is what moved the telegraph decay out of this teaching level and into HEAT DEATH.

name: HEAT DEATH
summary: Level 6, dl 610 onward with end:Infinity: THE EYE opens it, nothing new is taught, and the Infinity end is what makes the finale block skip it entirely.
detail: LV row 6. The finale latch is guarded by lvEnd<1e9, so an Infinity end means no star dive and no level completion - play simply continues. The owner retired the rule that the last level must stay endless; the comment beside the row calls Infinity a placeholder until the next level is built, not an endless-mode rule.

name: LV
summary: The six-row level table: each row is {dl0, end, name, key, mech}, and LEVEL_MAX is LV.length rather than a literal.
detail: Windows are dl 0/90/215/340/470/610 with end:Infinity on the sixth. key is a frequency ratio (1, 0.8909, 0.7937, 0.7071, 0.6300, 0.5612) that scales the SFX pentatonic. LEVEL_MAX is declared immediately after the table so loadPrefs can clamp cometloop:gl against it. check.mjs asserts finish lines strictly increase; smoke.mjs asserts LEVEL_MAX===LV.length.

name: dl() per-level rebase
summary: dl() returns the level's own dl0 plus a ramp re-run from zero at every level, so difficulty-seconds are absolute across the game but the gentle opening repeats per level.
detail: base = LV[G.level-1].dl0; the age term is (age()+min(G.diff*0.22,40))*MD().clock, and the first 80 seconds of each level advance at 0.55 rate before switching to 44+(a-80). So a level-4 start is dl 340 on its first frame, and the nudge good play earns is capped at 40. In the lab dl() is pinned to LAB_DL=40, chosen because it is exactly TIERS[3].at (THIRD RING) - three orbits - and level 1's finish line at 90 is then unreachable.

name: level finish line and the star dive
summary: A level ends by latching the finale 10 dl-seconds early at a quiet musical moment and laying 11 trail stars plus a sun; with no WebAudio it completes bare at the finish line instead.
detail: Guarded by lvEnd<1e9 and !bhActive(). The latch needs no live finale, no starfall, dl()>=lvEnd-10 and a quiet payoff (MU.pay<=0 && !MU.rise). The trail is 11 stars 0.55 rad apart walking the cadence [4,3,2,4,3,2,1,3,2,1,0], four on the outer ring, four mid, three inner; the sun sits one step further and only blooms once the melody is nearly gathered, so the ending is always a deliberate dive. levelComplete() rolls the upgrade offer, banks carryScore/orbits/lands/streak/groove/time and fires level_cleared.

name: the level card
summary: State lvend draws the level card: a level number and name, then either three upgrade tiles on a real advance or a one-line tip and a LEVEL n button on a retry or a picked start.
detail: Three entries: levelComplete() sets {done:true,next:level+1} and calls rollOffer(); retry() sets {done:false,next:G.level} for level 2+; startFromSelect() sets {done:false,next:n} when the device has no runs yet or n>=2. cardDone() commits G.level and reports card_shown with the seconds it was read. A level-1 retry, and a level-1 start by a player who has run before, skip the card entirely.

name: LV[].mech (mostly dead)
summary: LV[].mech has one reader: the card's tip line reads mech[0][1] only, and only for levels 2-6, so level 1's three rows and every level's rows past the first never render.
detail: The only read is const tip = n===1 ? 'Learn the controls as you play.' : (L.mech[0]&&L.mech[0][1]) || ... . Level 1's card substitutes a hardcoded string, so its ['swipe',null] row - annotated 'resolved at draw time by swipeWords()' - is never resolved by anything. That tip is also the else branch of `offered`, so on a real level advance the upgrade tiles take the slot and no mech line shows at all. The comment above LV says the card lines are checked against MECHANICS.md; check.mjs's ledger guard reads TIERS and LAB_ORBS names only.

name: LEVEL_HOME
summary: Each level floors the sky journey at its own world - [0,1,2,3,4,7] into WORLDS - so a level never sends a travelling player backwards and every level has a distinct opening image.
detail: Applied as G.skyW=Math.max(G.skyW,LEVEL_HOME[...]) in startGame, and the journey itself survives a level boundary - only a fresh run zeroes G.skyW. VEIL (index 5) and GRID (6) are deliberately not homes: they are travelled through between REDSHIFT and HEAT DEATH by orbiting. The inline comment beside the array names VEIL for index 2, which is wrong - WORLDS[2] is DUSTLANE.

name: per-level orb guarantees
summary: spawnPow() is an ordered if-chain of level gates: hypernova and slipstream from level 2, magnet and star trail from 3, the mirror and the black hole offer from 4, scorch from 5.
detail: Order: lab override, the POW_INTRO trio, the pity shield at sinceShield>=3, the level-4 black hole guarantee, the 5% black hole roll from level 3, then hyper, mirror, scorch, spot, slip, trail, then the POWPOOL roll. Each guarantee is once per RUN - the flags survive level boundaries and are pre-spent for any home level behind the level a run opens on. The fallback roll respects the same level floors and renormalises over the eligible rows, so a first run on LIFT OFF cannot be handed the magnet.

name: black-hole guarantee scope
summary: Level 4 guarantees the black hole is OFFERED once per run, not taken: bhPlaced marks the offer spent and a decline arms a 20s cooldown, after which only the ordinary 5% roll remains.
detail: The guarantee branch requires level>=4, !bhRun, !bhPlaced, G.t>=G.bhCool and !bhActive(). Placing it sets bhPlaced, bhRun and bhCool=G.t+20. bhRun is cleared only when carried is false - a genuinely fresh run, not a level advance - which is what makes the guarantee once per run rather than once per level. Unlike every other orb it is a real choice with a cost either way, so a guarantee to OFFER is the only kind it can carry.

name: silent tier pre-climb at a level start
summary: A level-2+ start (and the lab) sets G.tier=tierIndex() and raises G.nRings from the tiers below it before the first frame, so no banner fires for rungs the level opens past.
detail: Two lines: G.tier=tierIndex() and a loop taking the max of TIERS[i].rings for i<=tier. The card is the announcement instead. The same two lines give the lab its three rings from LAB_DL. tierIndex()'s twin hold is exempted for level>=2 by the level rather than by forging didHop, so the hop hint, the rehearsal and the death coach stay honest about what this run's thumbs actually did. skyI is recomputed by the same formula the in-run ratchet uses, clamped to the four sky bands.

name: the level picker and G.startLevel
summary: From the second run on, a picker offers all six levels; the choice is never persisted and G.startLevel>1 disables the deepest-level record and tags the share text.
detail: startFromSelect() clamps to LEVEL_MAX, sets G.level and G.startLevel, clears the upgrade state and every carry counter, then shows the level's card - or starts instantly at level 1 for a device that has runs. Rows the device has reached are marked Reached via G.lvlMax. G.newLevel, which drives FURTHEST YET and the cometloop:gl write, requires !LAB.on && G.startLevel===1, so a picked run can never move the record; the share text adds ' - from Ln' when startLevel>1.

name: G.tier vs G.level
summary: Two ordinals: G.tier is the thirteen-rung unlock ladder and speaks only through banners and telemetry; G.level is the 1-6 structure and owns every string the player reads.
detail: levelName() returns LV[G.level-1].name and feeds the HUD standing line, the death-screen subtitle and the share text. tierLabel() walks back to the nearest named rung and is read by telemetry only. runSummary() prints LEVEL n/LEVEL_MAX with one pip per level, filled to the level this run reached. The rule exists because the header once read LEVEL 4 next to a tier name seconds after the card said EVENT HORIZON: an earlier session tried to fix that by renaming the tier, and the collision came back one level later, because the defect was printing two ladders side by side.

name: what survives a level boundary
summary: startGame() runs at every level advance as well as every fresh run, and `carried` is the one switch deciding whether score, journey, guarantees, first-time flags and the intro trio reset.
detail: Kept when carried: the score - restored, with the layer ladder seeded from it - the sky journey G.skyW, orbits/lands/bestStreak/bestGroove, bhRun, the six orb-guarantee flags, didReverse/didHop/didLap, saidChor and introN. Cleared regardless: G.tier and G.nRings before the pre-climb, the board, the shield bank, groove and build state, PAUSE, chorusN/chorusBars and the started clock - so per-level and per-run are two different scopes inside one function. G.runs++ also fires here, so run_index advances at every level boundary.

name: carried = !!G.carryScore
summary: The level-boundary signal is a score, not a flag: startGame reads const carried=!!G.carryScore, so a clear banked with a zero score would be handled as a fresh run.
detail: The line is read directly at src/game/runtime.js:6136; the consequence is reasoned. levelComplete() sets G.carryScore=G.score, and every carry decision downstream - journey, guarantee flags, didHop, introN, bhRun, the chorus naming line - keys off the truthiness of that number. A run that reached a finish line having scored nothing would therefore re-arm the whole beginner path on the next level. The star dive pays before levelComplete, so the only reachable route is the no-WebAudio path, which completes bare at the finish line with no dive.

name: level prose vs source
summary: Where the level docs and the runtime's own comments disagree with LV and TIERS - the stale halves are listed in the note, and source wins in every case.
detail: Live at this commit: LEVEL_HOME's inline comment names VEIL for index 2 where WORLDS[2] is DUSTLANE; MECHANICS.md's claim that check.mjs reads level 2's finish line as ends[1] describes code that no longer exists; two runtime comments still describe the pre-six-level ladder; and docs/design/levels.md's unlock table quotes an older generation of every banner sentence, including the two rungs renamed to SHUTTERS and SHUTTER PAIRS.

name: plain shard (single)
summary: The opening formation at tier dl 0: one shard, shape rank 0, the fallback every rejected placement downgrades to.
detail: TIERS[0] carries name:null, so it has no banner - the MEET lesson and the level-1 card do the teaching. mkSpike defaults are life rand(2.6,4.4), scaled 0.7 while age()<30, and a warn stretched forward to the next eighth-note so the arming lands on the grid. Every failed gate, funnel, saucer or diver becomes a single rather than a skipped spawn.

values.lesson: Red hits cost a shield; tap to turn or swipe rings

name: TWIN SHARDS (twin)
summary: dl 18: two shards on one ring 0.30-0.40 rad apart, wide enough that the answer must be a hop rather than a late reverse; capped at two live pairs from dl 340.
detail: Both halves take the same heading-aware clearance or the pair could straddle the comet. Each shard is stamped tw:'twin' so a twin death coaches the hop instead of reporting 'single'. The ladder holds at SECOND RING until the first hop lands (see the hop hold), because twins are the tier that makes the hop compulsory. From dl 340 pickType refuses a twin while four tw-stamped shards are live - a twin places two shards from one clear spot, which made it the cheapest shape on a crowded board and 62-65% of everything standing on levels 5 and 6.

values.lesson: Two red obstacles: swipe to another ring

name: GATES (gate)
summary: dl 100: the same angle blocked on every ring, so hopping cannot save you and the answer is a tap; vetted at spawn for somewhere to reverse into.
detail: reverseEscape(GATE_ESCAPE) requires one whole ring clear for 1.1 rad along the post-reversal heading; failing it downgrades the spawn to a single rather than shipping a trap. Placement needs every ring clear at the angle and at least 1.7 rad from the comet. While any gate segment is live behindPad() returns 0, so the no-spawn bubble goes symmetric and a later spawn cannot invalidate the escape the gate promised. One wall at a time, and never on a board with a saucer.

values.lesson: A wall blocks every ring; tap to turn around

name: DRIFTERS (drift)
summary: dl 128: a shard given a fixed random heading of 0.24-0.50 rad/s, well under player speed; it never steers and never chases.
detail: va is applied in updateSpikes as s.a += s.va*sdt, and the hit tolerance is widened by the distance travelled this frame. The chevron sprite's point leads the motion. Both earlier wordings for this shape named behaviour it does not have - 'these ones chase you' and 'keep moving', the second of which names no input, since there is nothing in this game that stops you.

values.lesson: This red obstacle moves; tap to turn away

name: SHUTTERS (blink)
summary: dl 165: a shard that cycles on a two-beat grid at 0.55 duty - a solid red crystal while armed, four hollow shutter blades while open, closing as re-arm approaches.
detail: Renamed from BLINKERS in the effects pass; the type key is still 'blink'. armed(s) is blinkPhase(s) < BLINK*duty(s) with BLINK = two beats and BDUTY = 0.55, so it is lethal for 55% of each cycle. The read is geometry rather than opacity: artifactShard draws the solid shard sprite when armed and, when open, four blades at constant alpha 0.78 whose inner radius closes as the cycle runs out. Shutters are also excluded from the bloom halo pass, so the danger is never signalled by a toggled glow.

values.lesson: Pass through the open shape; avoid solid red

name: SLIDING GATES (driftgate)
summary: dl 240: a gate whose every segment shares one drift of 0.18-0.34 rad/s, so the wall crowds the exit shut and the reversal has to come early.
detail: A compound, not a new object: it is the gate branch with a non-zero va. Every segment must take the SAME drift or the rung shears away from the bar, which is drawn from one anchor segment's angle. It shares the one-wall-at-a-time slot and the reverseEscape check with plain gates, and its drift is deliberately slower than a lone drifter's - a sliding wall should crowd the exit, not chase you down.

values.lesson: The wall moves; tap to turn before it reaches you

name: THE SAUCER (saucer)
summary: dl 275: the only shape placed against the player, holding station 0.55 rad off the tail; turning triggers a one-beat charge and a 0.42s ring-wide shot, and its body is never solid.
detail: Skips the placement loop entirely - there is one position it can take. saucerOK() requires nRings>=2, G.t>=G.sauT, and no live saucer or gate. Three states with no easing: glued to the tail, frozen and charging with s.a untouched and `side` flipped so its world angle is unchanged, then firing. The charge cannot be cancelled by turning back, and it fires at the ring it is standing on. Contact reads s.saucer ? s.fire>0 : sweptHit(...), so only the shot is a hitbox. Not compound.

values.lesson: Turning triggers its shot; swipe to another ring

name: SHUTTER PAIRS (blinktwin)
summary: dl 310: a twin whose halves run at duty 0.5 offset half a cycle, so exactly one side is solid at every instant and the other is always the gap.
detail: Renamed from FLICKER PAIRS; the type key is still 'blinktwin'. Built in the twin branch with blink:true, duty:0.5 on both and bo:BLINK*0.5 on the second. Duty 0.5 rather than the lone shutter's 0.55 is what makes the lesson literally true - at 0.55 both sides were armed for 10% of every cycle, so a player who waited for the gap died in it. smoke.mjs walks a full period at 120 samples and requires exactly one armed member throughout.

values.lesson: The shapes take turns opening; pass through the open one

name: DIVERS (dive)
summary: dl 395: the only shard whose ring is not the ring it armed on - it transfers to an adjacent orbit 55% of the way through its own telegraph.
detail: Placement rejects the spawn outright unless BOTH the lane it leaves and the lane it lands in are clear - an unreadable arrival is neither fair nor survivable, so it is not downgraded the way a gate is. The transfer fires at s.t >= warn*0.55 and sets s.ring = s.diveTo, with an arc flash on the ARRIVAL ring and a note in the level's key; the remaining 45% of the warn is the lesson. Needs two orbits, so pickType skips it at nRings<2.

values.lesson: It moves to the marked ring; swipe to another ring

name: THE NARROWS (funnel)
summary: dl 520: a wall across every ring but one, answered by a hop where a gate is answered by a tap; the open lane is always adjacent to the comet and never its own ring.
detail: Placed against the player's ring, so it does not use the gate's reverseEscape check - the escape it must guarantee is a lane, not an arc. The open lane is held to 2.2 rad of player clearance against the walls' 1.7, because a shard sitting in it turns the formation from a demand into a trap. Drawn as contiguous runs of blocked rings with the gap left as a visible hole plus two comet-coloured brackets opening into it; the `bar` tag marks the one segment each run is drawn from, since a funnel may not have ring 0.

values.lesson: Swipe to the ring with no wall

name: TIERS
summary: The thirteen-rung unlock ladder keyed to dl: at 0/12/18/40/100/128/165/240/275/310/395/520/610, three of which announce a ring or the exam rather than a shape.
detail: Rows are {at, type, name, sub|subFn, rings}. Three rows carry type:null - SECOND RING, THIRD RING and THE EYE - and TIERS[0] carries name:null so it has no banner. Every sub is byte-identical to its type's MEET lesson, which smoke.mjs enforces. tierIndex() answers the clock; G.tier is a ratchet that advances at most one rung per frame and only when the crossing gates allow it. T_VOICE and T_SKY are derived from the table by NAME rather than by ordinal, after inserting DIVERS and THE NARROWS moved THE EYE from index 10 to 12.

name: SECOND RING / THIRD RING
summary: The two tiers that add an orbit rather than a shape: ring 2 at dl 12 and ring 3 at dl 40, each raising G.nRings and each carrying a filter lift the player can hear.
detail: A crossing with T.rings > G.nRings raises the ring count, draws two expanding rings and plays a rising pair. RINGS[].lift climbs 0/380/820 going in, which is the real reward - angular speed is one G.speed with no radius term, and an ember pays the same on every ring, so the retired THIRD RING banner claim of 'faster and higher' was two false claims. SECOND RING's sub is computed by swipeWords() so it follows whichever swipe rule the device chose. A second ring landing for a player who has never hopped also opens the once-ever hop rehearsal.

name: THE EYE
summary: The last rung, dl 610 on level 6's floor, with type:null - it adds no shape and no ring and exists to mark the end of teaching.
detail: Its sub can never render in-run: dl 610 is also level 5's finish line, so a level-5 crossing falls inside the suppressed endgame window, and a level-6 start pre-climbs G.tier before the first frame. It was renamed from STORM because tierLabel() returned it as the level-4 header label seconds after the card said EVENT HORIZON, and it moved from dl 340 to 610 with the six-level ladder rebuild.

values.sub: Collect stars and complete orbits to score

name: the compound formations
summary: gate, blink and drift (va) are independent flags on one shard and update/draw already handle any combination, so SLIDING GATES and SHUTTER PAIRS cost a spawn branch each and nothing else.
detail: Only two combinations are actually spawned. Two constraints make them work: a sliding gate gives every segment the same drift, or the rung shears apart from the bar drawn from one anchor segment; and a shutter pair is offset exactly half a cycle at duty 0.5, so there is always exactly one gap and never two. The death classifier reads the same flags back to name the killer.

name: MEET
summary: One sentence per formation, byte-identical to its tier banner's sub, shown once per device when the shape first spawns; smoke.mjs fails the build if the two ever drift apart.
detail: Every entry is {t, g, soft?}. Threat lessons are hard - the world dilates to 0.06x under a veil with the specimen spotlit - and reward lessons carry soft:1, because dilation is protection from threats, not ceremony for gifts. firstMeet() is called at each spawn SUCCESS site, never before the placement loop, so a failed placement cannot spend the once-ever lesson. The ten formation sentences are the values below.

values.single: Red hits cost a shield; tap to turn or swipe rings
values.twin: Two red obstacles: swipe to another ring
values.gate: A wall blocks every ring; tap to turn around
values.drift: This red obstacle moves; tap to turn away
values.blink: Pass through the open shape; avoid solid red
values.driftgate: The wall moves; tap to turn before it reaches you
values.saucer: Turning triggers its shot; swipe to another ring
values.blinktwin: The shapes take turns opening; pass through the open one
values.dive: It moves to the marked ring; swipe to another ring
values.funnel: Swipe to the ring with no wall

name: stale lesson quotes in the docs
summary: Every one-sentence lesson quoted in docs/design/levels.md is a previous wording; the code's banner subs and MEET lessons are identical strings and smoke.mjs keeps them that way.
detail: The docs' unlock table still prints the pre-rewrite generation - 'harmless while dim - cross it then', 'only one is solid - cross the dim one', 'no new tricks - just more of everything' and nine more. The shipped sentences all name a verb the game has and its observable consequence. Two of those rows are now doubly stale, because their rungs have since been renamed SHUTTERS and SHUTTER PAIRS. The docs' claim that a sub is word-for-word the lesson remains true in code; only the sentences they print are wrong.

name: BLINKERS -> SHUTTERS, FLICKER PAIRS -> SHUTTER PAIRS
summary: The two cycling formations were renamed and re-worded in the effects pass; the type keys blink and blinktwin did not change, and three places still carry the old names.
detail: Moved together: the TIERS names and subs, the two MEET lessons, T_VOICE's findIndex on 'SHUTTERS', the MECHANICS.md rows, and the draw, which now says danger with shape rather than a toggled halo. Did NOT move: tools/curriculum.mjs's expected banner ladder still lists BLINKERS and FLICKER PAIRS, and because it skips names it cannot find, two rungs dropped silently out of that ordering check; docs/design/levels.md and docs/design/ladders.md still print the old names; smoke.mjs's pair-alternation comment still says FLICKER PAIRS. check.mjs's ledger guard passes because both new names appear in MECHANICS.md.

name: the new shape insists
summary: While any unlocked shape's lesson has not landed, that shape - lowest tier first - IS the next spawn, so the curriculum promise is not left to pool odds.
detail: pickType walks k=0..top and returns the first unseen type, after the same exclusions the pool loop applies. The newest shape gets a 4-second head start so its banner lands before its first specimen. Veterans have seen everything, so the loop never runs for them, and density is untouched - same spawn, different shape. curriculum.mjs plays a whole headless climb and fails the build if any of the sixteen taught things is still unseen at the frontier.

name: featuredTier and the newest-shape tripling
summary: The newest shape gets two extra pool copies once its rung has been up ~18s; featuredTier walks back past ring-only rungs so a new ring never quietly makes the board easier.
detail: Keying the tripling off the top rung directly meant the three type:null rungs featured nothing: crossing THIRD RING dropped gates from 60% of the pool to 33%, and the last rung - whose own banner promises more of everything - flattened the shutter pair from 33% to 14%. featuredTier(top) walks down to the last rung that carries a type. The ~18s delay is why you meet one drifter before you meet three; G.featT is reset at every crossing and at startGame.

name: SHAPE_RANK and the late-board mix
summary: From dl 340 to dl 900 complexity earns pool weight: w = 1 + round(hb * SHAPE_RANK[type] * 1.5), with hb exactly 0 below level 4's floor so levels 1-3 are untouched.
detail: Ranked by how many independent facts the player must read: a single is a position, a twin a position and a count, a gate a wall and a verb, a diver a position that changes, and the compounds and the saucer two behaviours at once. This is the axis the back half escalates on, because density is saturated - measured mean live shards were 8.42 / 9.19 / 9.23 across levels 4, 5 and 6, a 10% rise across two whole levels.

name: formation exclusions
summary: Five rules decide what pickType may offer: one wall at a time, no wall beside a saucer, no saucer without its cooldown, nothing needing two rings at nRings<2, and at most two live twins from dl 340.
detail: The gate/saucer exclusion is the load-bearing one: a gate exists to force a reversal and the saucer exists to price one, so the pair could demand a move and punish it in the same breath. It is held apart in the pool rather than solved by placement, because there is no placement that makes them compatible. gate, driftgate and funnel share the one-wall slot; twin, blinktwin, dive and funnel all need nRings>=2. Both the insist loop and the pool loop carry the same five filters, duplicated on purpose.

name: farFromAll, behindPad and the relaxing separation
summary: Eighteen placement attempts per spawn: shard-to-shard separation relaxes to 55% across the sequence, while the player clearance never relaxes because it is the reaction-time guarantee.
detail: Clearance is expressed as multiples of hit width ((18.5*u)/radius radians), so it holds on every ring and every screen. The player term follows travel: the full clearance ahead along the heading and only behindPad() behind, which is 0.16s of travel floored at 0.45 rad - and 0 while any gate is live, so the bubble goes symmetric and the gate's promised escape cannot be invalidated. Rewards keep the old symmetric clearance, so the arc behind a stationary player gets colder rather than richer.

name: the twin hold at SECOND RING
summary: On level 1 the ladder holds at rung 1 until the first hop lands, then resumes where the clock says; after 30 difficulty-seconds the twin arrives anyway so the hold cannot be farmed.
detail: Conditions: !G.didHop, G.level<2, !LAB.on, state playing, and i>1. G.holdD is stamped once at first engagement; releasing on the timeout sets G.holdTimeout, the purest telemetry signal that the hop lesson never landed. Clamped inside tierIndex rather than in the ratchet, so pickType and the banner can never disagree about the tier. Speed, shard cap and spawn rate still run on dl() untouched - the gate changes what arrives, never how much - and the lab is excluded because its frozen clock would jam the release valve forever.

name: when a tier crossing may fire
summary: G.tier advances one rung at a time and only when six conditions hold: no finale, no live banner, no black hole, no hard lesson, and not inside the level's last 10 dl-seconds.
detail: The guard is ti>G.tier && !FIN.on && !FIN.pend && !G.banner && !bhActive() && !(G.teach>0 && !G.teachSoft) && !(lvEnd<1e9 && dl()>=lvEnd-10). Each clause was added after a collision: a banner over a star dive, one over the singularity, one over a lesson's frozen veil, and the pile-up that skipped every banner but the last. Any crossing a boundary swallows is owned by the next level's silent pre-climb, because that level's card is the announcement. Only THE EYE at dl 610 actually falls inside an endgame window (level 5's), and it carries type:null - no other rung sits within 10 dl of a finish line.

name: the unseen type's 1.6x telegraph
summary: A formation the device has never seen telegraphs at warnTime()*1.6 on its first specimens, computed before firstMeet stamps the seen bit so the shard teaches alongside the sentence.
detail: Applied at five spawn sites - saucer, funnel, gate/driftgate, drift, blink and dive - as `const w = G.seen[type] ? {} : {warn: warnTime()*1.6}` merged into the shard. The single and the twin get no extension. It matters because a lesson may defer for calm while the shape still spawns: the longer warn is the channel that survives a deferred sentence.

name: G.lastHit formation priority
summary: A killed player's formation is decided by one nested ternary over the shard's flags: saucer, then wall (funnel, sliding, plain), then diver, then the twin stamp, then shutter, drifter, single.
detail: Order matters because the flags combine: a sliding gate is gate+va, a shutter pair is blink+tw. The tw stamp is what lets a twin death coach the hop - a lone shard cannot infer which formation it came from, so twin deaths used to report 'single' and the coach went silent for the exact formation that forces the unfamiliar verb. die() then looks the value up in MEET for the death coach, and re-arms that lesson if the device has seen it once but not twice.

name: the pre-rebuild ladder comments
summary: Two runtime comments still describe the three-level ladder: one says the whole ladder fits inside levels 1-2, the other counts ten tiers and names the last rung STORM.
detail: The first gives a wall-clock spacing table for gates through flicker pairs inside level 2 and says the four storm shapes 'now land inside level 2 (dl 75-190)'; the table twenty lines below it puts SLIDING GATES at 240, THE SAUCER at 275, SHUTTER PAIRS at 310, DIVERS at 395, THE NARROWS at 520 and THE EYE at 610. The second is featuredTier's header. Neither is behaviour - featuredTier derives its answer from the table - but levels.md itself states the rule that a comment describing intentions is the same defect as a rule disagreeing with its enforcement.

name: THE EYE's claimed harness pin (absent)
summary: Two comments say smoke.mjs pins the last tier's `at` to a level boundary. No such assertion exists anywhere in tools/ - the rung's dl 610 is unguarded.
detail: smoke.mjs touches TIERS at 343 (ordering and finiteness), 346 (every type has a MEET entry), 354 (sub matches lesson) and 723 (mode invariance); none compares a tier's at to a level boundary. check.mjs only asserts tier unlocks are non-decreasing and level finish lines strictly increase. curriculum.mjs only checks that G.tier has caught up to the clock. A grep of tools/ for THE EYE returns nothing. One of the two comments is doubly stale: it still says 'a dl 340 crossing', written when THE EYE sat at 340.
